newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fedex gets US go-ahead for Vietnam charter flights.
newsitem.headline: Fedex gets US go-ahead for Vietnam charter flights.

text.p: Federal Express Corporation has been granted permission by the U.S. government to begin charter flights to Vietnam, a Hong Kong-based Fedex spokesman said.

In April 1995, shortly after Washington lifted its trade embargo on Vietnam, Fedex airlifted charity relief supplies and became the first U.S. carrier to return since the end of the Vietnam war, the spokesman told Reuters.

Linking up with the company's Subic Bay hub in the Philippines and adding Vietnam to the integrator's Asian network is not yet possible as there is no bilateral agreement between Hanoi and Washington, and any flights will be on an ad hoc charter basis only, he added.
Fedex does not have any firm plans for the number of flights or their frequency, the spokesman said.

Industry sources said the Fedex go ahead is another step towards an aviation treaty which would allow scheduled air links between the two former enemies. Four hundred and fifty U.S. companies are estimated to have established themselves in Vietnam where the economy is growing rapidly along with demand for express parcel deliveries.

"We are open for business in Vietnam and awaiting charter work. We were the first U.S. carrier to return to Vietnam with the charity relief airlift a couple of years ago and we are now looking forward to flying there a lot more often," the spokesman said.

Fedex already has offices in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City and currently uses scheduled airlines to connect with its worldwide network, the spokesman added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
